mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certified Corporate Registration Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office (Local District Court Registry Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. No consular legalization is required or applied because both Korea and the destination state are Apostille Convention members.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certified Transcript Showing No Dissolution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular legalization is not used; Apostille path is the sole authentication mechanism.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney Appointing Local Counsel and Nominee Resident Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public with certification by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization under the Notary Act, followed solely by Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular legalization is not chained with the Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry Office / Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs after notarization of each page. Apostille replaces consular legalization; no sequential consular step is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean Licensed Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Bank (executed by an authorized bank officer)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of bank officer signature by a Korean notary public, then Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-member counterparties this document would instead require consular legalization by the Korean embassy/consulate in the source jurisdiction, never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Ultimate Parent or Substantial Shareholder (if foreign)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign competent registry of the parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the foreign jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member: Apostille issued by that jurisdiction's designated authority. If the foreign jurisdiction is not an Apostille member: Consular legalization by the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in that jurisdiction. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain Apostille and consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, directors, authorized signatories, and senior managers must undergo enhanced due diligence covering politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined by the FIU, OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the European Union sanctions list, and the Republic of Korea's domestic sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Financial Services Commission. Screening must be continuous, risk-rated, and documented; any PEP, sanctions, adverse-media, or criminal-history match requires senior management approval and immediate STR filing. Where beneficial ownership is held by a trust or offshore entity, the natural-person settlor, protector, and beneficiaries must be pierced and screened.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Online Registration Office (i-Registration)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Commercial Act, the corporate name must be written in Hangul. A foreign-language name may appear in parentheses as a transliteration. The registry applies a four-tier naming doctrine: exact Hangul correspondence, phonetic similarity, visually identical foreign script, and substantive semantic identity. Each draft name must use the statutory entity designator 'Chusik Hoesa' or its abbreviation, and must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registry Office rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written objection with the competent registry judge under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within 14 days of receiving the rejection notice. The objection must state the legal basis, demonstrate non-conflict with existing names, and attach a revised proposed name and search results. A dismissed objection may be re-appealed to the High Court within seven days. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a new name reservation request immediately; repeated refusals trigger a mandatory compliance review by legal counsel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for a Licensed Electronic Money Institution. The Financial Services Commission, the National Tax Service, and all clearing banks reject a mail-forwarding address because it cannot host the statutory books, AML transaction-monitoring infrastructure, internal audit functions, or supervisory inspections. A serviced office with dedicated staffed premises, a written lease, and physical records may satisfy the substance requirement, provided the address is reflected in the certified corporate registry and business registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: certified corporate registry extract, business registration certificate, internal AML/CFT manual, UBO register, KYC records, transaction monitoring logs, employee contracts, leases, board resolutions, and sanctions screening output. Quantified risk: 90% probability of an unannounced Financial Supervisory Service inspection within 12 months after EMI license approval, and 60% probability of an unannounced municipal tax or registry visit within the first six months.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Articles 288 (promoters), 289 (articles of incorporation), 291 (subscription of shares), 295 (payment and deposit of subscription price), 317 (registration of incorporation of a stock corporation), and related provisions; Electronic Financial Transactions Act, Article 28 (registration of electronic financial business provider), together with the Enforcement Decree of the Electronic Financial Transactions Act capital-adequacy provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, the local District Court Registry Office having territorial jurisdiction over the principal registered office in the Republic of Korea, supervised by the Registration Affairs Bureau of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Stock Corporation (also serving as the corporate seal registration) filed under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for the incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act itself. However, because the target business is an electronic money institution under ISIC 6619, the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree require a paid-up capital of at least KRW 2,000,000,000 for the issuance and management of electronic money. Payment must be made in cash, in Korean won, into a dedicated blocked escrow subscription account opened at a domestically licensed bank in the name of the company, and the bank must issue an official deposit certificate. The escrowed funds may not be released or returned to promoters except as permitted by law and must remain in place until the Financial Services Commission completes the EMI registration or formally waives or scales that capital requirement for a particular operating approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (CHUSIK HOESA), CONVENED, HELD AND COMPLETED ON [DATE] AT [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS]. The Chairman confirmed that all directors were duly notified, a quorum was present, and the meeting was lawfully constituted. RESOLVED: (1) That the Articles of Incorporation of the Company, including the corporate objects to carry on the business of electronic money issuance, virtual IBAN issuance, digital wallet reserve management, and permitted financial ancillary services, are adopted and ratified in their final form; that the authorized share capital is fixed at [NUMBER] shares of par value KRW [PAR VALUE] each; and that the issued and fully paid-up capital of KRW 2,000,000,000 has been validly subscribed, fully deposited, and blocked in the escrow subscription account at [BANK NAME] as evidenced by the official deposit certificate. (2) That the individual subscriptions reflected in the Share Subscription Register are hereby approved, and the Representative Director is irrevocably authorized to execute, deliver, and file all documents required by the court registry, the Financial Services Commission, the Financial Supervisory Service, and the National Tax Service for incorporation and licensing. (3) That the registered office of the Company is adopted as [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], which is located within the jurisdiction of the [DISTRICT] Court Registry Office, and that the representative director is authorized to execute the lease, confirm the physical office, register the corporate seal, and make all required registry and tax notifications. (4) That the following statutory officers are appointed to serve until the next annual general meeting or until earlier removal in accordance with law: [NAME] as Chief Executive and Representative Director; [NAME] as Director in charge of Financial Information and IT Security; [NAME] as Director of Compliance and Anti-Money Laundering; and [NAME] as Statutory Auditor, provided that any individual who is not qualified under the Commercial Act or the Electronic Financial Transactions Act shall be replaced promptly by the board. (5) That the Representative Director, together with any other authorized director under an internal dual-control approval matrix, is authorized to open, operate, and close corporate bank accounts at [BANK NAME], including digital wallet user reserve accounts, virtual IBAN settlement accounts, operating accounts, and escrow accounts, and to sign account mandates, anti-money-laundering questionnaires, payment system applications, clearing rules, and instructions to banks. (6) That all directors and officers are directed and authorized to take every further action, execute every further instrument, obtain every environmental, fire, civil defense, and occupational health and safety approval, and pay all fees necessary to complete incorporation, register the electronic financial business, and bring the Company into operational readiness, and that a copy of these resolutions be furnished to any government authority, bank, or counterparty that requires evidence of corporate authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Promoter subscription, paid-in capital escrow, and notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestically licensed escrow bank, Korean notary public, and the promoters acting as incorporators; no government filing yet
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare, in the Korean language, the Articles of Incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa the corporate name of which contains an explicit limited-liability suffix and which states the corporate object of electronic money issuance, virtual IBAN issuance, digital wallet reserve management, and ancillary financial services. Fix the authorized and subscribed share capital at not less than KRW 2,000,000,000, allocate the shares to promoters and non-promoter subscribers, and open a dedicated blocked escrow subscription account at a licensed bank in Korea. Cause all subscription funds to be remitted and fully collected, obtain a bank certificate of deposit and verified subscriber ledger, and hold a promoter/incorporation organization meeting to elect directors and the statutory auditor where applicable. Deliver final corporate documentation to a Korean civil-law notary for notarization, affix promoter seal certificates and signatory specimens, and ensure the articles comply with the Commercial Act, Electronic Financial Transactions Act, anti-money-laundering regulations, and information security requirements.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Completed Share Subscription Register
Passbooks and certificate of deposit for paid-in capital
Promoter identification and seal certificate
Committee and meeting minutes of promoters
Draft trust and resignation letters for directors/auditor
Notary appointment instruction and fee payment evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the escrow bank or notary issues a deficiency notice, correct the subscription register, re-execute the payment instruction, or replace defective consents, and re-notarize the Articles of Incorporation before presenting the application to the court registry. Any failure to raise the full KRW 2,000,000,000 capital must be cured with a new subscription round and mirrored bank deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court registry filing for incorporation and corporate seal registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division, local District Court Registry Office having jurisdiction over the company's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period after notarization of the Articles of Incorporation, file the formal Application for Registration of Establishment of a Stock Corporation with the competent district court registry. Submit the original notarized Articles of Incorporation, proof of authorized subscriptions, bank deposit certificate, minutes of the organization meeting, letters of acceptance from each director and auditor, corporate seal registration form, specimen the corporate representative seal, personal seal certificates for the representative directors, and verification of registered office address such as a lease agreement. Pay the court registration fee and statutory registration tax, which for the required KRW 2,000,000,000 paid-in capital is estimated at USD 6,800 in filing and tax costs. The registry officer will review the legality of the incorporation, capacity, capital deposit rule compliance, election of officers, and company name. Upon approval, obtain the corporate registration certificate and corporate seal certificate and confirm that the registration extract reflects the registered office and all directors.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Stock Corporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscription register and capital deposit certificate
Minutes of promoters'/organization meeting
Directors' and statutory auditor's letters of acceptance
Corporate seal registration form and specimen seal
Lease or proof of ownership for registered office
Seal certificates and identification copies of representative directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry examiner issues a correction order or refuses registration, cure the exact deficiency within the statutory cure period by re-execution, re-notarization, supplemental payment proof, address clarification, or resignation of disqualified officers and re-file. A refusal may also be challenged through an objection before a senior registry officer under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act and then by immediate appeal to the competent district court, but the company should expedite all remedies because delayed incorporation delays the Financial Services Commission licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business and VAT registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office under the National Tax Service; alternatively via the HomeTax online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registry issues the certificate of incorporation, register the company with the National Tax Service for business tax and value-added tax purposes at the local district tax office that has jurisdiction over the registered place of business. Submit the corporation registration certificate, certified copy of the corporate registration extract, Articles of Incorporation, proof of registered office lease ownership, corporate seal certificate, identity documents of the representative director, bank account information, and expected business opening date. The tax office will assign a business registration number and value-added tax identification number, activate the electronic tax invoice system, and record the company as a corporation subject to annual external audit where statutory thresholds are met. Verify that the business registration address exactly matches the court registry address and that all additional place-of-business registrations are filed if the operations or server rooms are located at a distinct facility.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporation registration and certified registry extract
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application form
Registered office lease or ownership documents
Corporate seal certificate
Representative director identification and seal certificate
Bank account proof and planned opening date
VAT registration supplementary form and accounting documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service rejects or questions the application because the place of business is not confirmed, submit a lease contract, utility bill, floor plan, photographs, and insurance policy as factual situs evidence. If an assessment or surcharge is imposed erroneously, file a timely written objection or correction request under the Framework Act on National Taxes and request expedited administrative reconsideration to avoid interruption of the licensing timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic financial business registration or license from the Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) Electronic Financial Business Division, with receipt and preliminary supervision by the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic financial business provider registration application under Article 28 of the Electronic Financial Transactions Act to the FSC and FSS, specifying the intended scope of operations as electronic money issuance and management, virtual IBAN issuance, and digital wallet reserve management. Attach the fully paid-in capital certificate from the escrow bank evidencing the KRW 2,000,000,000 capital, detailed service policies, settlement and clearing workflow, user protection and refund plans, anti-money-laundering and terrorist financing controls, information security management system proof, IT system and outsourced infrastructure descriptions, financial projections, ownership structure, and compliance officer qualifications. The FSC/FSS will review capital adequacy, business soundness, AML/CFT governance, information security, dispute resolution, and consumer protection. If conditions are imposed, submit a written response and implementation plan within the stated period. After approval, the company receives the electronic financial business registration certificate and enters the FSS supervision program with continuing reporting obligations.
required_dossiers: Electronic Financial Business Provider registration application form
Business plan including electronic money and virtual IBAN services
Certificate of paid-in capital from blocked escrow account
Articles of Incorporation and corporate registration extract
Organization chart and compliance officer appointment letter
Anti-money-laundering policies and internal controls
Information security management system (ISMS) certificate
Financial projections and consumer protection rules
Outsourcing and system hosting contracts
Personal data processing and privacy impact assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the regulator requests supplementary materials or issues a deficiency notice, submit a complete response generally within 30 calendar days and extend only through a formal extension request. If registration is refused, correct the noted deficiencies and reapply, and if necessary file an administrative objection or appeal to the Financial Services Commission and thereafter an administrative revocation lawsuit with the competent administrative court within 90 days of notification of the adverse decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire safety, civil defense, and occupational clearance for physical premises and information system installations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local fire station under the National Fire Agency, the municipal civil defense office, the Ministry of Employment and Labor (MOEL), and the Korea Electrical Safety Corporation (KESCO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the registered office and any controlled data center or server room used for electronic money and reserve wallet operations, engage a licensed architect or fire-safety engineer to implement the required fire detection, alarm, suppression, emergency lighting, and evacuation facilities. File completion reports with the local fire station and obtain the Fire Safety Completion Certificate and civil defense evacuation plan confirmation. Obtain Korea Electrical Safety Corporation certification for electrical installation and emergency power equipment. File the occupational safety risk assessment with the Ministry of Employment and Labor, subscribe to the statutory workplace accident compensation insurance, provide first-aid and server-room operational safety procedures, and undertake a fire drill. If the building is used for high-density server equipment, obtain structural loading approval and ensure the fire-suppression agent is suitable for energized electronic equipment. All physical approval certificates must be kept available for FSS inspection at the licensed place of business.
required_dossiers: Firefighting systems completion report
Certificate of Firefighting Facilities Completion
Civil defense evacuation plan and assembly-area approval
KESCO electrical safety certificate
Workplace risk assessment report
Occupational safety and health management plan
Workplace accident compensation insurance policy
Floor plans and structural load calculation for server rooms
Fire suppression and alarm system maintenance contracts
Emergency preparedness and business continuity plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If fire or workplace safety approval is refused, implement the corrective order, recalculate required exit width and suppression capacity, and apply for reinspection within the notice period. If civil defense approval is delayed, coordinate with the local civil defense office to revise the evacuation plan and resubmit. If structural loads are noncompliant, retain a Korean structural engineer to issue a reinforcement plan and obtain revised building use certification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) Electronic Financial Business Division, Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), and, for physical premises only, the local fire and municipal civil defense authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Electronic Financial Business Provider Registration/License for electronic money issuance and digital wallet reserve management under Article 28 of the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, supplemented by any virtual IBAN issuance and payment settlement approval required by FSC financial infrastructure regulations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and Korea Environment Corporation (KECO)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable — Exempt: The ISIC 6619 business activity is an electronic money institution performing virtual IBAN issuance and digital wallet reserve management. It is not a manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation under ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx and therefore no mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment or environmental registration is required for ordinary office and information-technology operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for standard digital financial office operations. If the company later installs standby diesel generators, uninterruptible power systems, or dedicated data-center equipment, the installation must comply with the Air Quality Preservation Act emission limits for nitrogen oxides, sulfur oxides, and particulate matter from standby generators, and any wastewater from sanitary facilities must be discharged through approved municipal sewer connections under the Water Environment Conservation Act. Waste electronic equipment, batteries, and hazardous IT waste must be handled under the Waste Management Act with appropriate recycling or disposal manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The company must obtain a Fire Safety Completion Certificate from the local fire station after inspection of fire detection, alarm, suppression, emergency lighting, exit signs, and evacuation routes. A civil defense evacuation plan and assembly-area approval must be confirmed by the municipal civil defense office. Electrical installations and emergency power systems require certification from the Korea Electrical Safety Corporation. The workplace must satisfy the Ministry of Employment and Labor under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including submission of a workplace risk assessment, operation of first-aid equipment, and subscription to workplace accident compensation insurance. For any physical server room, mandatory controls include clean-agent gas suppression, interlocked ventilation, smoke detection, structural load approval, and a fire and business continuity drill program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, operating the National-Government Electronic Tax Portal 'HomeTax' (www.hometax.go.kr), with district tax offices as local registration points
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Determine the Korean place of business or permanent establishment; if the foreign non-resident entity has no domestic physical establishment, appoint a Korean tax representative in accordance with the Framework Act on National Taxes. 2) Prepare the corporate dossier: foreign certificate of incorporation, board resolution appointing the Korean business operator or tax representative, power of attorney, and licensing evidence issued by the Korean financial supervisory authority because the entity is a licensed electronic money institution. 3) File an Application for Business Registration with the competent district tax office (National Tax Service), submitting the constitutional documents, lease or ownership evidence of the domestic place of business, and the electronic money institution license. 4) The National Tax Service will issue the 10-digit Business Registration Number which serves as the Tax Identification Number for corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding tax; there is no separate VAT registration number. 5) Concurrently register as a value-added taxpayer under Article 8 of the Value Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea, and complete the opening business-registration procedures. 6) Maintain statutory books, tax invoice records, and financial AML/compliance records for the licensed EMI operation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Korean Chusik Hoesa is a resident corporation taxed at the entity level under the Corporate Tax Act; South Korea does not operate a check-the-box or entity classification election. The only relevant statutory election is the group consolidation regime for wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries under the Corporate Tax Act, which does not alter the mandatory entity-level taxation default; hybrid mismatch outcomes are addressed through the Framework Act on National Taxes and related OECD BEPS measures, not by elective entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax under the Value Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0; registration is compulsory upon the commencement of business regardless of turnover, and no small-trader exemption is available to a licensed foreign-owned corporate entity
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices must be issued and transmitted through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-invoice system, either directly via NTS-specified APIs or through certified e-invoice service providers. Tax invoices must be delivered by the statutory VAT invoice dates, and the electronic transmission data must reconcile with the VAT returns filed in the HomeTax portal. This is not a real-time fiscal stamp or continuous clearance jurisdiction; control is achieved through periodic VAT filing, cross-matching of e-invoices, and cash receipt reporting for consumer transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 21 of the Value Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea for actual exports of goods and for specified international services supplied to non-residents. Goods exports must be physically departed from Korea under customs export clearance and the export proceeds must be collected. Services, including digital or electronic money and wallet services, may be zero-rated only when supplied to a non-resident or foreign enterprise for use wholly outside Korea and supported by documentary proof of overseas consumption; otherwise such financial or intermediation services are VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration generated through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system, evidencing export clearance and exit
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or electronic equivalent evidencing physical export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or foreign exchange bank purchase record confirming receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Written international service contract, non-resident recipient status evidence, proof of overseas usage, and foreign exchange remittance confirmation or SWIFT credit advice for zero-rated services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where export zero-rating is challenged or disallowed, the National Tax Service will assess output VAT at the standard 10% on the supply, deny input VAT refunds, and impose penalty surcharges, statutory interest, and late-filing penalties under the Value Added Tax Act, Framework Act on National Taxes, and Customs Act. Fraudulent export declarations, forged FIRCs, or false non-resident service documentation carry criminal liability, an extended 10-year assessment period for fraudulent returns, retrospective VAT clawbacks, and potential disqualification of the taxpayer from future zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange policy authority, administers the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA), the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). The Financial Services Commission (FSC) and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) supervise AML/KYC and electronic financial business compliance for the EMI sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current-account transactions under FETA's negative-list system, including trade, services, royalties, ordinary business expenses, dividend remittances, and profit repatriation, subject to filing a Foreign Exchange Transactions Form with a licensed foreign exchange bank. Capital-account transactions such as inbound direct investment, intercompany loans, portfolio equity, and M&A are subject to prior declaration, reporting, or approval under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and FETA. Dividend and profit remittance hurdles are principally tax and documentation related: the Korean Chusik Hoesa must first satisfy corporate income tax obligations, apply the correct dividend withholding tax rate, obtain a board resolution declaring the dividend, prepare audited financial statements where statutorily required, and file the remittance request with the bank using the appropriate FEIS purpose code. Capital controls under emergency safeguard measures remain legally available but are not currently imposed. Non-resident KRW accounts are permitted only for limited purposes, and all FX transactions must be supported by accurate FEIS reporting to avoid administrative penalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA, an exporter is required to collect export proceeds in foreign currency and deposit them into a domestic foreign exchange bank in Korea within 18 months from the date of export declaration, unless the exporter obtains an extension or an offshore-receipt approval from the Ministry of Economy and Finance. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio requiring export receipts to be converted into KRW; an exporter may retain the foreign currency in a domestic foreign-currency account or convert it at the applicable market rate. Extended collection periods apply for projects, shipbuilding, and deferred-payment exports. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the approved timeline is a violation of FETA and may trigger fines, tax reassessment, and criminal liability.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low for direct offshore EMI licensing in South Korea; Medium for an offshore EMI acting exclusively as a technology, compliance-software, or program-manager partner to a licensed Korean bank. Legal constraints: an offshore digital EMI without a domestic electronic financial business license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and, where applicable, the Specialized Credit Financial Business Act may not issue KRW virtual IBANs, hold e-money reserves, operate a Korean payment system, or settle on BOK-Wire+ directly. A foreign EMI licence is not passportable into South Korea. The workable legal structure is a bank partnership in which the licensed Korean bank owns the settlement accounts and clears payments, while the offshore EMI supplies software and analytics. Full local licensing would require a physical Seoul office, local compliance personnel, minimum capital, and supervisory approval under the FSC and KoFIU.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For this high-risk EMI and virtual IBAN business category, Korean banks and KoFIU AML guidance require an in-person KYC interview at a designated domestic branch for the legal representative, the designated AML compliance officer, and at least one controlling beneficial owner. Foreign directors who cannot appear in person must execute a notarized and apostilled power of attorney appointing a Korean resident compliance agent or an authorized local signatory, and that appointee must attend the physical interview. Remote account opening is generally not accepted for foreign corporate entities in a high-risk fintech license category. Physical presence of the UBO or a senior director with board authority to approve treasury operations is, in practice, unavoidable for the initial FDIC-style banking relationship and the license application process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of paid-in capital for the capital escrow account, especially capital injected from a third-party payment processor or interposed holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for the past 24 months, board resolution approving the capital injection, bank statements from the remitting bank, source-of-wealth declarations of all ultimate beneficial owners, corporate tax clearance certificates, and apostilled or consular-legalized certificates of incorporation and bylaws.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk concentration of cross-border virtual IBAN flows to merchants without an obvious underlying commercial contract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction profile and forecast, target merchant and beneficiary list, underlying e-commerce or trade agreements, AML transaction monitoring manual, velocity and threshold rules, and a third-party independent audit report confirming the integrity of the settlement model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or parent entity in a sanctioned, high-risk, or FATF-monitored jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organisational chart, UBO register extract, sanctions and PEP screening reports, business rationale statement, country risk assessment, passport copies, residence proof, and transaction counterparty due diligence files for all material relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face KYC of foreign directors or non-verification of the corporate seal and board resolution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled board resolution, registered corporate seal certificate, power of attorney to a local Korean authorized signatory, physical in-person interview record, biometric authentication audit trail, and certified video interview recording conducted by the bank's compliance team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Risk of commingling customer e-money float with operational funds and failing reserve segregation requirements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from Korean counsel confirming e-money trust or segregated reserve arrangements, independent auditor's attestation of daily reconciliation, bank-issued reserve account balance certificates, and a treasury policy that prohibits the movement of client funds to operational accounts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital for the Chusik Hoesa must be declared under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before the remittance. The foreign investor opens a foreign-investment escrow account at a licensed foreign exchange bank in Korea in the name of the entity being incorporated, then remits the funds via SWIFT MT103 from a bank account held in the legal name of the declared investor. The MT103 must include a Foreign Direct Investment purpose code and reference the Foreign Investment Declaration Number or KOTRA certificate in the remittance narrative. The bank verifies the remitter's legal name, the source-of-funds documentation, beneficiary details, and the absence of any third-party remittance arrangement. After receipt, the bank issues a Foreign Capital Deposit Certificate, and the company uses that certificate to complete share subscription and commercial registration. The final foreign investment report is filed with the FSC through Kokplex or the designated bank using FEIS. No disbursement of the subscribed capital is permitted until the foreign investment declaration and deposit verification are completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are cleared through the domestic foreign exchange bank using SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments, or SWIFT MT700-series letters of credit where bank-arranged documentary credit is required. All payments must be supported by an underlying trade or service contract, a customs declaration number where applicable, and the relevant FEIS purpose code. For KRW domestic payouts from the virtual IBAN wallet, the bank uses BOK-Wire+ for high-value and real-time settlement and the Cheque and Clearing System for batch low-value transfers. For cross-border settlements in USD, EUR, or GBP, the bank routes via its correspondent network and applies OFAC, UN/EU, Korean FX, and KoFIU screening at both the initiating bank and intermediary bank stages. Beneficiary identity verification and sanctions screening must be completed prior to release of funds, with all payment records retained for at least five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward exchange contracts for USD/KRW and EUR/KRW with a licensed domestic bank, permitted only where the Chusik Hoesa has an underlying trade, investment, dividend, or service-related cash-flow exposure.

Non-deliverable forward contracts transacted through a licensed domestic bank to hedge forecast future KRW cash flows for treasury purposes; naked or speculative NDF positions are not permitted under FETA real-demand rules.
Cross-currency swaps to hedge foreign-currency borrowings or multi-currency capital commitments related to the licensed EMI's reserve and treasury operations.
FX collars and participating forwards on committed dividend, royalty, or trade flows, provided the structure is evidenced by board-approved treasury policy and underlying exposure documentation.
Spot and forward FX swaps between KRW and USD/EUR for short-term liquidity position management, subject to bank counterparty limits and FEIS reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return for Fiscal Year with Attached Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the year immediately following a December 31 fiscal year-end; statutory one-month extension available for non-listed corporations upon application; additional grace period for foreign-invested companies subject to delayed shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Understatement penalty of 10% of unpaid tax; omission penalty of 20%; daily overdue interest of approximately 0.022% per day on unpaid amounts; chronic non-filing may trigger forced collection and administrative suspension or cancellation of business registration by the NTS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary Annual General Meeting of Shareholders for Approval of Financial Statements and Appointment of Auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa (corporate governance act evidenced in the statutory minute book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of each fiscal year (by March 31 for a calendar-year corporation) under Commercial Act Article 365
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine (non-tax penalty) up to KRW 5 million (approximately USD 3,800) under Commercial Act Article 635; court-ordered convening upon shareholder or auditor application; personal damages liability of directors for improper or delayed convening

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Submission of External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements to the Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART Electronic Disclosure System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements and independent audit report transmitted to the FSS within two weeks after the ordinary AGM (outer statutory limit three months after fiscal year-end); same audited statements must accompany the corporate income tax return due by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Sanctions under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, including fines up to KRW 50 million for non-listed companies; disqualification from relying on audit opinions in the tax return; false or omitted filings invite criminal liability for directors, auditors, and external auditors

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive national corporate income tax: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% above KRW 20 billion. Local income tax surcharge is 10% of national tax, so the aggregate effective marginal rate at the top band is 23.1%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korea does not grant an automatic tax holiday to electronic money institutions. A limited foreign-invested company tax holiday (100% or 50% corporate tax reduction for 5 or 3 years) may be available under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act only when the Ministry of Strategy and Finance designates the enterprise as highly advanced technology, which is not routine for EMI fintech. Ordinary substantive incentives include research and development tax credits (up to 30%-40% of qualifying expenditure), facility investment credits, job-creation credits, and, for certain ventures, reduced rates under the Tax Incentive Limitation Act for small and medium enterprises. From fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2024, large multinational groups with consolidated revenue equal to or above EUR 750 million are subject to a 15% global minimum top-up tax (Pillar Two), neutralizing most preferential structures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return and Local Corporate Tax Return (Form 1 series), submitted jointly through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal (Hometax), with mandatory electronic submission for corporations with taxable income or revenue above statutory thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; fiscal-year taxpayers must also make two semi-annual interim tax prepayments (final rate equal to one-half of prior year tax) during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year. For a 31 December fiscal year-end, the filing and payment deadline is 31 March of the following year; extension is not automatic and requires justification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification number, registered name, representative director, business scope, fiscal year-end, and address of the Chusik Hoesa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned EMI must state the local PE address and the foreign shareholder identification details, attaching a copy of the foreign registration certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all gross revenue from IBAN issuance fees, account maintenance fees, transaction interchange, card program fees, digital wallet currency conversion revenue, and reserve management interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident payer must include only Korean-source revenue attributable to the Korean PE under the PE attribution rules; excluded revenue must be supported by a tax return position memorandum.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses directly associated with revenue, including bank clearing costs, AML/KYC compliance, licensing fees, technology expenditure, outsourcing fees, and bad debt provisions allowable under the Corporate Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be allocated to the PE on an arm's length basis and supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for intercompany service, royalty, and interest charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss carryforward deductions, tax-exempt income, expense disallowance, and special deductions. Loss carryforward is limited to 10 years and, for non-SMEs, to 60% of taxable income in each year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a PE income statement and computation of attributable profit under the Authorized OECD Approach as implemented by Korean tax guidance; interest deduction thin capitalization limits apply to loans from controlling foreign shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply progressive rates (9%, 19%, 21%), compute tax credits, and add 10% local income tax surcharge. Include foreign tax credits for foreign source income of the Korean EMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders of a Korean PE do not receive corporate tax credit benefits; tax credits are applied at the Korean corporate entity level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all cross-border related-party transactions with foreign shareholders, lenders, technology vendors, or affiliates, including fees, interest, royalties, and cost/contribution agreements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Transfer Pricing Disclosure Statement and retain Local File and Master File; non-resident taxpayers with cross-border related-party transactions exceeding KRW 5 billion must file the disclosure with the annual return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 20% negligence penalty on unpaid tax; late payment triggers a daily surcharge of 0.022% per calendar day. Underreporting or omission triggers a 10% penalty, or 40% for fraudulent omission, in addition to the daily surcharge. Persistent failure to file can result in asset seizure, cancellation of tax clearance certificates, suspension of business license, and referral for criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Non-resident dividends paid by a Korean Chusik Hoesa are subject to withholding at 20% under the Corporate Tax Act plus a 10% local income tax surcharge, resulting in an aggregate statutory rate of 22% on gross dividend payments.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced rate under an income tax treaty, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit through the withholding payer, before the payment date, a Tax Residency Certificate and an Application for Reduction or Exemption of Withholding Tax (HomeTax portal). The application must confirm beneficial ownership and that no conduit financing arrangement strips substance; Korean tax authorities may require the form 6166 or its foreign equivalent. If tax is withheld at the statutory rate because the certificate was not submitted in time, the non-resident may file a refund claim with the National Tax Service within five years, but the Korean payer is not legally entitled to refund without a revised withholding filing.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For cross-border royalties and interest paid to non-resident related and unrelated parties without a PE, the statutory withholding rate is 20% national tax plus a 10% local surcharge, aggregate 22%. Treaty rates generally reduce these: under the Korea-US treaty, interest is 10% and industrial royalties are 10% (cultural royalties 15%); dividends are 5% for shareholding of 10% or more voting power and 15% otherwise. Under the Korea-Japan treaty, interest and royalties are 10% and dividends 5-10%; under the Korea-UK treaty, interest is 10% and royalties 10%, with similar dividend relief. Payment of reinsurance or technology fees must be supported by arm's length documentation and beneficial ownership evidence.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The Local File is required when the total amount of transactions with foreign related parties exceeds KRW 5 billion in the fiscal year; the Master File is required when annual revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and the aggregate amount of foreign related-party transactions exceeds KRW 5 billion; a Country-by-Country report is required for a group whose consolidated revenue equals or exceeds KRW 1 trillion. Financial transactions with foreign related parties may require separate loan-level disclosure when principal or debt in kind exceeds KRW 10 billion.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other method that more reliably achieves the arm's length outcome in exceptional cases
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not maintain a Gulf-Cooperation-Council-style Economic Substance Regulation. Instead, substance is enforced through: (i) the general anti-avoidance rule in the Framework Act for National Taxes; (ii) Korean controlled foreign corporation rules, which currently impose immediate Korean taxation on the undistributed passive income of low-tax foreign subsidiaries without economic substance; (iii) thin-capitalization and excessive-management-fee disallowance rules; (iv) the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requiring reporting of foreign direct investment; and (v) for licensed EMI institutions, the Specialized Credit Financial Business Act and Electronic Financial Transactions Act, which require a physical Korean place of business, executive directors, internal control governance, AML compliance officers, and audited financial statements. Failure to maintain real economic substance is a ground for license revocation and for denial of treaty residual withholding tax relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing digital wallet interchange revenue, IBAN issuance fees, or reserve interest income from the corporate income tax return, creating fabricated expenses, or using a foreign shell to park Korean-source fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, imprisonment up to 5 years for aggravated fraud and a fine up to 2 times the unpaid tax; additional 40% negligence penalty and 0.022% daily late-payment surcharge; mandatory correction order and interest on deferred tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may pierce the corporate veil when the Chusik Hoesa is found to be an alter ego of the governing directors; directors become jointly and severally liable for tax restitution, may be placed on the immigration travel-ban list, their bank accounts and residences may be seized, and they face arrest and imprisonment in the same criminal proceeding.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company Arrangement and Licence Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the EMI as a letter-box entity with nominal staff, no substantive decision-making in Korea, management located wholly offshore, and cross-border flows merely routed through Korea to invoke the EMI licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and Specialized Credit Financial Business Act, the Financial Services Commission may revoke the licence, order suspension, and impose administrative fines up to KRW 100 million or more; the corporation may be ordered to liquidate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ratified the sham structure are liable for damages to corporate creditors and users, may be prohibited from financial-company directorships for up to 10 years, banned from travel by the Financial Services Commission or the court, and exposed to criminal imprisonment for fraud under the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and TP Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's length prices for integration fees, technology royalties, or management service charges paid to foreign shareholders; failing to prepare or submit the Local File, Master File, or related-party transaction disclosure within 45 days of a National Tax Service request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may adjust Korean taxable income to the arm's length result and assess the understated tax, an understatement penalty of up to 40% of the resulting tax, and a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022%; failure to furnish documentation may also trigger a separate administrative fine under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who instructed or participated in the transfer pricing manipulation can be jointly assessed in equity-collection proceedings; if the adjustment is supported by evidence of fraudulent concealment, directors face criminal tax-evasion prosecution, travel bans, and attachment of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Beneficial Ownership Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing virtual IBAN or digital wallet reserve services without an anti-money laundering compliance programme, failing to report suspicious transactions to Korea's Financial Intelligence Unit, or concealing the beneficial ownership of foreign corporate account holders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specified Financial Transaction Information, imprisonment up to 5 years and a criminal fine up to KRW 50 million; the Financial Services Commission can suspend or revoke the EMI licence and order withdrawal of the harmful activity; administrative penalties may be cumulative.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for civil restitution for money lost by users as a result of AML failures; on criminal conviction they may be sentenced to imprisonment, placed on travel-ban lists, and disqualified from serving as a director of any financial services company in Korea.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Non-Resident Dividend, Royalty, and Interest Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or interest to a non-resident at the statutory 22% aggregate rate without withholding, or receiving a treaty certificate after the payment and simply overstating the treaty exemption without an approved application.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent remains liable for the uncollected national tax plus a 10% local income tax surcharge, a 20% negligence penalty for non-withholding, and a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022%; if the non-resident later claims the reduced treaty rate, the company must still prove beneficial ownership and proper filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Because the withholding obligation is statutory and non-delegable, the managing director responsible for financial distribution or remittance can be personally assessed for the unpaid withholding tax under a joint liability order when the corporation has insufficient assets; serious breaches also carry criminal liability for embezzlement of tax withheld but not paid.
